_readme: Calibration baseline for the curriculum coverage analyzer.
Lives in scripts/ and IS COMMITTED. The fixtures themselves are third-party
copyrighted syllabi and stay gitignored in fixtures/calibration/ -- but this
file contains only filenames, languages and expected numbers, which is our
regression baseline and the most valuable artifact in the exercise.
TWO KINDS OF EXPECTATION, KEPT SEPARATE ON PURPOSE:
hand_*   what a human judged by reading the document. An anchor, NOT an
oracle. Where the engine and a hand score disagree, the matched
span decides -- see tuv-sud below, whose hand score was the thing
that turned out to be wrong.
expect_* the current engine baseline. Asserted on every run. A change here
is a REGRESSION unless a migration or code change deliberately
caused it, in which case update this file in the same commit.
sha256_16 is the first 16 hex chars of the SHA-256 of the .txt fixture.
It guards against a silent re-extraction: a pdf-parse upgrade that changes
the text would otherwise present as an engine regression.

fixtures.notes: BOTH gates fail. Precedence test: framework mismatch outranks density because a different object model tells a reader more than a short document. The hand coverage of 14% is recorded but must never be stored -- a CHECK in migration 219 makes that impossible.

Closest direct competitor. THE REGRESSION GUARD THAT MATTERS: this document returned drift=0 cleanPass=true until the ruleLangs default was fixed, because every rule is en and the document is es-419. English rules must fire on Spanish sources -- the official Spanish Guide keeps roles and artifacts in English. If this ever reads 0 again, the language routing has broken.

Syllabus V1.2 dated May 2020; the 2020 Scrum Guide published November 2020, so the edition lag is structural rather than negligent. Only fixture with published weights -- 21 reverse gaps and 23 review items are the sole real test of the weight extractor, and those have NOT been read individually yet. Went 4 -> 5 -> 4 across migrations 221 and 222; the transient 5 was a section number masquerading as a count.

OPEN GAP: hand 6 vs engine 3. Not yet diagnosed. Migration 221 was written to close it and did not -- Scrum roles was already firing via the heading, not via the count. Do not widen another rule to chase this number without first identifying WHICH three terms the hand score counted.

78-page manual, not a syllabus -- a different KIND of input, and 9x the size of anything else in the corpus. Never hand-scored. Only document detected as hybrid, which is the correct verdict for partially-updated material. Carries the only Sprint Zero hit, from the rule that was dead until the self-match assertion caught it.

THE HAND SCORE OF ZERO DRIFT IS WRONG AND IS KEPT ONLY AS A RECORD. The document carries 'Sprint Planning meeting', 'Sprint Review meeting' and 'Sprint Retrospective meeting' as literal rows in its own weighting table, and 'enable participants to live Scrum roles' in its qualification criteria. Both verified against the PDF. Tuning a rule until it agrees with an estimate is how a detector becomes decorative. Segment is certification_body, so outreach_disposition must be do_not_contact -- a peer, not a prospect. Allocates 1% to the Scrum Master role against D5 at 22.5%.
